title: ‘नैकापे सर्किनी’ कथामा शक्तिसम्बन्ध "Naikape Sarkini" Kathama Shaktisambandha
nepali: प्रस्तुत आलेख पारिजातको ‘नैकापे सर्किनी’ कथामा निहित शक्तिसम्बन्ध विश्लेषण गर्न केन्द्रित छ ।पाश्चात्य क्षेत्रमा विकसित साांस्कृतिक अध्ययनको अन्तर्गतको सीमान्तीयतासम्बन्धी चिन्तनमा शक्तिसम्बन्धकोअवधारणालाई महइभ्वका साथ हेरिन्छ । साहित्यमा यो नवीन समालोचना पद्धतिका रूपमा विकसित छ । अन्तोनियोग्राम्सीले प्रभुत्वसम्बन्धी मान्यताको परिचर्चाका क्रममा अघि सारेको शक्ति सम्बन्धको अवधारणा फुकोलगायतकाविद्वान्को विचारबाट परिपोषित छ । समाजमा अस्तित्वमा रहेका विभिन्न वर्ग, जाति, लिङ्ग, धर्म, संस्कृति तथाक्षेत्रीयताका बीचमा शक्तिको के कस्तो सम्बन्ध रहेको छ भन्ने कुरालाई शक्तिसम्बन्ध भनिन्छ । यस आलेखमाशक्तिसम्बन्ध सम्बन्धी मान्यताका आधारमा ‘नैकापे सर्किनी’ कथाको विश्लेषण गरी निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ ।मुख्यतः शक्तिसम्बन्धका वर्ग, धर्म, जाति र संस्कृति जस्ता सैद्धान्तिक आधारमा पाठ विश्लेषणात्मक पद्धतिकोअनुसरण गरिएको यो गुणात्मक लेखमा विवेच्य कथामा प्रयुक्त कथ्य र सहभागीको अवस्था र समाजमा रहेकोशक्तिसंरचना र विभिन्न वर्गको हैसियतको विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । मूलतः पुस्तकालयीय विधिका आधारमा तथ्यकोसङ्कलन गरेर निर्धारित कथाको विषयविश्लेषण गरिएको यो लेख शक्ति सम्बन्धका विषयमा खोज गर्ने अनुवर्तीखोजकर्ताका लागि उपयोगी हुन जान्छ । ‘नैकापे सर्किनी’ कथामा वर्गीय रूपमा उच्च वर्ग र माथिल्लो भनिएकाजातिले समाजमा प्राप्त भएको सम्पूर्ण शक्तिको उपभोग गरेको तर निम्न वर्ग र तल्लो मानिएका जाति यसबाटपूण वञ्चित भएको स्पष्ट हुन्छ । लैङ्गिक रूपमा पुरुष हैकमका कारण नारीहरू शक्तिहीन र अधीनस्थ बनेकाछन् । सांस्कृतिक दृष्टिमा कथामा चित्रित समाजमा उच्च संस्कृतिको दवदवा रहेको र निम्न संस्कृति नियन्त्रितभएको छ । यसर्थ ‘नैकापे सर्किनी’ कथामा उच्च वर्ग, पुरुष सत्ता र उच्च संस्कृति र यसका मान्यताहरूको सत्ताकायम भएको हुनाले शक्ति उनीहरूको केद्रित रहेको र निम्न वर्ग, नारी समूह र निम्न संस्कृति नियन्त्रित रअधीनस्थ बनेको स्पष्ट हुन्छ ।
american_english: The present article focuses on analyzing the power relations embedded in Parijat's story 'Naikape Sarkini.' Within Western cultural studies, developed under considerations of marginality, the concept of power relations is examined with great emphasis. In literature, this has developed in the form of a new critical method. Antonio Gramsci, in the course of discussing the concept of hegemony, pushed the concept of power relations forward, and it has been nourished by the ideas of scholars including Foucault. The term power relations refers to what kind of relation of power exists among the various classes, castes, genders, religions, cultures and regionalities that exist in society. In this article, based on the tenets regarding power relations, an analysis of the story 'Naikape Sarkini' has been carried out and conclusions have been drawn. Mainly grounded in the theoretical bases of power relations such as class, religion, caste and culture, this qualitative article follows the textual-analytical method, and it analyzes the narrative used in the story under discussion and the situation of its participants, and the power structure prevailing in society and the status of the various classes. Fundamentally a subject analysis of the chosen story based on the library method and collection of facts, this article turns out to be useful for future researchers investigating the subject of power relations. In the story 'Naikape Sarkini,' it becomes clear that, in class terms, the upper classes and the castes called superior have enjoyed all the power available in society, while the lower classes and the castes considered inferior have been completely deprived of it. In gender terms, because of male authority, women have been rendered powerless and subordinated. From a cultural standpoint, in the society depicted in the story, high culture dominates and low culture has been confined. Hence it becomes clear that because in the story 'Naikape Sarkini' the reign of the upper classes, male power, high culture and their values has been established, power is concentrated in their hands, while the lower classes, the group of women, and low culture have been confined and made subordinate.

australian_english: This article centres on looking into the power relations built into Parijat's story 'Naikape Sarkini.' Within Western cultural studies, which have grown up around the question of marginality, the idea of power relations is taken very seriously indeed. In literature, it has developed as a new kind of critical method. Antonio Gramsci, while he was talking about hegemony, pushed the idea of power relations forward, and it has been built up further by thinkers including Foucault. What's meant by power relations is the sort of relationship power has among the different classes, castes, genders, religions, cultures and regions that exist in society. In this article, leaning on the thinking about power relations, the story 'Naikape Sarkini' has been analysed and conclusions drawn. Basically working from the theoretical bases of power relations like class, religion, caste and culture, this qualitative article follows the textual-analytical approach, and it analyses the narrative used in the story in question and the position of its characters, along with the power structure that holds in society and the standing of the various classes. Fundamentally built on the library method and the collection of facts to analyse the subject of the chosen story, this article comes out as useful for later researchers digging into power relations. In 'Naikape Sarkini,' it's plain to see that, class-wise, the upper classes and the so-called superior castes have had all the power society hands out, while the lower classes and the so-taken-for-granted inferior castes have missed out on it entirely. On gender, because of male authority, women have been left without power and put under. Culturally, in the society the story paints, high culture holds sway and low culture is kept under control. So it's plain to see that, because in 'Naikape Sarkini' the rule of the upper classes, male power, high culture and their values has been set up, power is concentrated with them, while the lower classes, the women's lot, and low culture are kept under and put underneath.
